A.explanation: 8 is the highest order on one side only, not the total count of $n = 0$ plus both $+n$ and $-n$ orders.

B.explanation: 9 counts $n = 0$ to $n = 8$ on one side only and misses the symmetric maxima on the other side of zero order.

C.explanation: 16 counts $8$ orders on each side but omits the $n = 0$ central maximum straight through.

D.explanation: Maximum order is $8$, so orders $-8$ to $+8$ give $8 + 1 + 8 = 17$ maxima, all in the forward semicircle.

hints: Notice the grating has 300 lines per millimetre, so first find the slit spacing $d$ in metres from $d = 1/300 \text{ mm}$.
Connect $d$ and the 400 nm wavelength with $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$ and set $\sin\theta = 1$ to find the largest possible order $n$.
Remember the semicircular screen in front of the grating catches the zero order plus every $+n$ and $-n$ pair up to that maximum $n$.
walkthrough: Find the grating spacing: $d = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}}{300} = 3.33 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
State the grating equation for normal incidence: $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$ with $\lambda = 400 \text{ nm} = 4.00 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
The largest order occurs at the largest angle $\sin\theta = 1$, so $n_{max} = d/\lambda = (3.33 \times 10^{-6})/(4.00 \times 10^{-7}) = 8.33$.
Only whole orders exist, so $n_{max} = 8$. That gives $n = 0, \pm 1, \pm 2, ... \pm 8$.
The view from above shows the screen covers the whole transmitted semicircle from $\theta = -90^{\circ}$ to $+90^{\circ}$, so all these forward orders land on it.
Total maxima $= 8$ on one side $+ 1$ central $+ 8$ on the other side $= 17$. This is option D.
